data.title: Twisted Speed
data.tagline: Race through the carnage and survive the onslaught. A thrilling racing game where both the players and the environment bite.
data.oneLiner: A racing game where you choose a vehicle (quick but light on weapons, medium build with moderate weapons, or heavy with tank-like weapons), choose a map (terrain, track, climate- each map will have it's own features that can slow/stop you) and then race to the finish.
data.elevatorPitch: Twisted Speed is a brutal 2D top-down racer where the track is a living predator and every rival is a moving executioner. Choose your rig—fragile speedster, balanced brawler, or armored crusher—then fight through a single cyber-Mex wasteland loop that actively tries to crush, electrify, or swallow you. The fantasy is simple: survive the onslaught, loot the wreckage, and return meaner for the next night run.
data.playerFantasy: Completed the race, upgrade your rig, live to see another day.
data.perspective: First person driver (through windshield or offset behind vehicle)
data.artPipeline: Grok Imagine batches (Unity CLI) + human review
data.audioDirection: Something fast paced (maybe choose a genre- Rap, Metal, Rock)
data.coreMechanic: Drive-and-destroy: hold throttle while aiming weapons and dodging active terrain traps
data.progression: Linear scrap economy spent on three upgrade trees (speed, armor, firepower) that persist across runs
data.combatOrChallenge: The track itself spawns moving hazards (collapsing bridges, electrified dunes, spike walls) that force constant positioning and resource decisions
loopSteps: Enter the neon-scorched garage and select your rig
Drop into the single living track as hazards awaken
Dodge, ram, and fire while the environment bites back
Eliminate or outrun rival vehicles before the finish line
Cross the line alive and collect scattered salvage
Spend scrap on targeted upgrades in the garage
Queue the next run with a deadlier build
stolenIdeas: The vehicle weapons and types from Twisted Metal Black
How the environment attacks you in Mario Cart
The racing dynamics in Need for Speed
The visuals and graphics from Need for Speed (especially newer ones)
v1Scope: One playable vehicle: the balanced brawler with front machine guns and rear rocket pods
Single 32-screen loop track: ruined highway through irradiated desert with three active hazards
Basic top-down driving with momentum, drift, and simple collision damage
Two weapon types that can be fired while moving
Three rival AI cars with basic aggression and targeting
End-of-run scrap screen and two upgrade choices
Pixel-perfect collision and 60 fps feel as the only polish target
openQuestions: Hook: the track is an active enemy that changes state every lap, turning racing into survival horror
Not clone: environment hazards move and target the player instead of being static obstacles like classic Twisted Metal
Deployment: start as single-player offline build for fastest vertical slice
Genres: pure racing-combat hybrid with no RPG elements beyond three upgrade paths
data.rawIdeas:
A dystopian world where you have to race to survive. Think about the movie Running Man, but this is a violent racing game where you are trying to win to gain your freedom or money or whatever the reason you are doing this. However, it's not just the players who are after you, the environment has also been designed to take you out. Vehicles can be equipped with guns, rockets, lasers, mines, etc. There is no perfect vehicle though, each have their pros and cons. Think about Mario where you can have a speedy motorbike but bad handling. So, between driving dynamics and weapons, the racer has to decide which vehicle best suits them. As the racer progresses through the maps/levels, they will level up and be able to upgrade their vehicles. If they find they picked the wrong vehicle for them, they can choose a new vehicle, but they will be starting from scratch with the upgrades.

AI risks & cuts:
Cut all rival AI behaviors beyond basic pursuit and ram
Remove second weapon type if driving physics slip
Drop end-of-run upgrade screen visuals to bare text list
Limit track to one hazard type if collision tuning takes too long
